key_insight: HSE’s screened hybrid design was created to make exact exchange practical in solids, and it unexpectedly became a highly effective way to improve band-gap predictions for semiconductors and some oxides.
engineering_relevance: Accurate band gaps matter for designing photovoltaics, power electronics, defect physics, and quantum-information materials, so HSE-like hybrids are widely useful in computational materials screening.
method: Use short-range exact exchange with long-range screening to keep hybrids affordable in extended systems.
Compare HSE03/HSE06 and newer semilocal, meta-GGA, dielectric-dependent, and tuned hybrid functionals on solid benchmarks.
Evaluate not only band gaps but also structures, energetics, cost, and transferability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that HSE band gaps for ordinary semiconductors and selected metal oxides came out substantially closer to experiment than semilocal approximations, and that HSE06 preserved good gap accuracy while improving molecular thermochemistry.
watch_item: Fixed screening and a fixed 25% exact-exchange fraction may not transfer optimally across all materials, motivating system-dependent tuning in some cases.
paper_title: Perspective: The HSE Screened Hybrid and the Band Gap Problem: Origins, Impact, and the Contenders
